t:
Section 42 of title 35, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:


“§ 42. Patent and Trademark Office funding

“(a) 
All fees for services performed by or materials furnished by the Patent and Trademark Office will be payable to the Commissioner.


“(b) 
All fees paid to the Commissioner and all appropriations for defraying the costs of the activities of the Patent and Trademark Office will be credited to the Patent and Trademark Office Appropriation Account in the Treasury of the United States, the provisions of section 725e of title 31, United States Code, notwithstanding.


“(c) 
Revenues from fees will be available to the Commissioner of Patents to carry out, to the extent provided for in appropriation Acts, the activities of the Patent and Trademark Office.


“(d) 
The Commissioner may refund any fee paid by mistake or any amount paid in excess of that required.”.

fable.w: This section only governs how Patent and Trademark Office fees are paid, credited to a Treasury account, made available through appropriation Acts, and refunded. The tempting reading is that fee payers interacting with the Commissioner, or the refund authority, amount to outside involvement, but paying fees is a transaction, not consultation on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: All fees for services performed by or materials furnished by the Patent and Trademark Office will be payable to the Commissioner.

qwen_block.w: This section outlines the financial mechanisms for the Patent and Trademark Office, specifically how fees are collected, credited to the Treasury, and used for office activities. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The interaction described is purely transactional (paying fees) and administrative (internal fund management), which falls under the 'No' category for applications/transactions and internal government operations.
qwen_block.s: All fees for services performed by or materials furnished by the Patent and Trademark Office will be payable to the Commissioner.

opus.w: This section only says how Patent and Trademark Office fees are collected, credited to an account, made available for spending and refunded. It sets up no public comment, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties or right to sue. The refund power in subsection (d) is an internal administrative decision, not a way for outsiders to take part in the decision.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that subsection (d), which lets the Commissioner refund a fee paid by mistake, sets up a process where outsiders interact with the agency. It doesn't. A fee refund is an administrative payment decision, much like an application for a benefit. No outside party is consulted before a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section deals exclusively with the internal funding mechanisms, fee collection, and appropriation accounts of the Patent and Trademark Office. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The interaction with the public described (paying fees) is part of the application process, which is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: All fees for services performed by or materials furnished by the Patent and Trademark Office will be payable to the Commissioner.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Patent and Trademark Office interacts with the public (inventors, companies) to process patent applications, this section involves participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" and "applications for... licenses." Processing patent applications is an administrative function, not a participatory decision-making process involving consultation or coordination with outside parties before a policy decision. Furthermore, this section is purely about internal funding mechanisms and fee structures within the federal government.
